title: SDK primitives for safe reconcile and rollback of batching recommendations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need a small, well-documented set of SDK primitives and control-plane endpoints that let downstream consumers (recs engine, autoscaling, customer-run scripts) safely reconcile batching and KV-cache recommendations and perform idempotent apply or automated rollback. The goal is to make config changes (batch size, cache TTLs, quantization profiles) consumable by automation while preserving strong safety guarantees: no partial applies left in a degraded state, clear audit trail, and a deterministic conflict-resolution model when multiple actors attempt concurrent changes. This ticket covers API design, SDK surface (client-side helpers + retry semantics), webhook handshake for external recommendation providers, and a lightweight transactional apply/rollback coordinator on the control plane. Focus on simplicity for early adopters and extensibility for future multi-resource transactions.
acceptance_criteria: A1: HTTP endpoints exist to create a recommended change bundle, preview diff, and request apply with a client-provided idempotency key.
A2: SDK exposes apply(), preview(), and rollback() helpers with clear retry/backoff guidance and automatic handling of idempotency tokens.
A3: Webhook contract documented: recommendation payload format, verification signature, acknowledgement/receipt semantics, and optional dry-run signal.
A4: Control-plane coordinates apply as an atomic commit per-bundle: either all settings in the bundle are activated or none are, with a persisted audit entry and rollback token on failure.
A5: Integration tests simulate concurrent applies from two actors and demonstrate deterministic winner selection and safe rollback on conflict.
A6: End-to-end demo with Optimize Recs UI: create rec -> preview -> apply -> observe runtime metrics revert on rollback.
A7: Documentation (Confluence + SDK docstring) and an example GitHub Actions workflow that uses the SDK to apply recommendations is published.
A8: Customer-facing error codes for common failure modes (conflict, validation, transient infra) are stable and documented.
A9: Telemetry events emitted for create/preview/apply/rollback with correlation id and idempotency key.
A10: Security review notes completed and no blocker mitigations outstanding (or documented compensating controls).
steps: Design API payloads and idempotency model; get PM/design sign-off (week 1)
Implement control-plane endpoints: POST /recs/bundles, POST /recs/bundles/:id/preview, POST /recs/bundles/:id/apply (with idempotency-key)
Add server-side coordinator that writes a single transaction record and runs validators then issues atomic commit or rollback token
Add SDK primitives for Node and Python: create_bundle(), preview_bundle(), apply_bundle(idempotency_key), rollback_bundle(rollback_token)
Define webhook handshake: initial POST from external rec engine, return 202 + bundle id, allow retry with same idempotency token; include signature verification example
Build integration tests for concurrency, validation errors, and full rollback path against staging runtime
Instrument telemetry and add per-route dashboard panels in Console
Publish docs, example workflows, and deprecation/compatibility notes
Run security review and update threat model and design accordingly
Soft-launch feature behind feature flag and run closed beta with two customers/Internal teams
notes: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting — alignment on atomicity: we treat each bundle as the unit of transaction; agreed to avoid multi-bundle cross-dependent commits in scope.
2026-02-25: Chose optimistic idempotency model where client-provided key is canonical; control-plane rejects duplicate non-matching payloads.
2026-03-02: Engineering review — debated strong serializable locks vs compare-and-swap; decided to use lightweight CAS on bundle record with retry window to avoid long locks.
2026-03-04: Design requested preview diffs to be human-readable and include estimated cost delta with confidence bands.
2026-03-08: PR #1349 opened for server endpoints; awaiting unit tests and integration harness updates.
2026-03-09: Ran chaos test that simulated lost ack from runtime during apply — coordinator now persists rollback_token and replayable operation log.
Tradeoffs: we accept eventual consistency across async runtime caches for performance; owners must provide explicit rollback when necessary.
Follow-ups: add native SDK helpers for automatic dashboarding of applied recs; later iterate on multi-resource transactions.
